title: MakerWorld Reviews
summary: Pulls every rating, comment, and nested reply from a MakerWorld model page into one translated, threaded JSON file with a working link per entry, and can turn it into a vibe dashboard.
what_it_is: A Claude skill that collects the complete **Reviews & Ratings** tab of a MakerWorld model: star ratings, comments, and every reply under them, however deep. Non-English posts are translated, and each entry gets a permalink that opens the model page with that thread pinned at the top.

The result is one JSON file (plus an optional plain-text thread tree). After delivering it, Claude offers a button to build Swami's vibe dashboard from the same file, with stats, a Q&A synthesis, critical feedback, every thread, the designer's replies, a search, a mind map, a glossary, and an audio overview.
why: MakerWorld loads reviews by script, 10 at a time, with replies hidden behind "View N more replies". WebFetch only sees an empty page and Claude's cloud workspace can't reach makerworld.com at all, so the data has to come from the site's own API, called from inside a real browser tab.

what_it_does.text: Pages through every top-level rating and comment, then every reply thread, from inside the model page's browser tab. It only reads; it never posts, likes, or replies.
Runs the extraction in the background and checks on it every 35 seconds, because each browser script call times out after about 45 seconds.
Compares what it got with the page's own **Reviews & Ratings (N)** count, and reports any small reply gap left by deleted replies.
Translates every non-English post into English and keeps the original text beside it, with short [bracketed] clarifications only where needed.
Writes `<model-slug>_makerworld_reviews.json`: a nested reply tree with dotted ids (12, 12.3, 12.3.1), plus a flat list of the same entries.
Gives every entry a link using MakerWorld's own `replyId` / `replyType` format, which opens the page at that thread (verified working Oct 2026).
Also writes `threaded.txt`, the whole thread tree in the original languages, delivered as the main output when Swami asks for "just the text".

On request, or from the button after delivery, builds a vibe dashboard from the JSON in the current vibe-dashboard format: stats (including ratings by print profile), common questions, critical feedback, rating and comment threads, designer replies, and contributors, plus the Search section, Mind Map, Glossary, References, and an audio overview.

triggers: "Get the reviews for https://makerworld.com/en/models/…" (or just paste the model link)
"Get the reviews **and** make a vibe dashboard" (extracts, then builds without stopping to ask)
"Make a dashboard from this JSON" (with a JSON this skill made earlier)
"Just the text" (delivers the plain thread tree alongside the JSON)

how_to_use.step: Start the chat in the **Claude desktop app** on the Mac, so Claude can use its built-in browser pane. Claude in Chrome (real Google Chrome with the extension) and Perplexity's Comet are the other supported browsers.
Paste the MakerWorld model link and say what you want: the reviews, the reviews and a dashboard, or just the text.
If the browser pane asks, approve access to makerworld.com. No sign-in is normally needed, because reviews are public.
Claude opens the model page, starts the background pull, and polls it until done (about one minute per 100 top-level posts).
Claude writes each data chunk into the page as plain text and reads it back into its workspace as `raw_NN.jsonl` files, then closes the tab.
Claude runs `build_reviews.py` once, translates the non-English posts into `translations.json`, and runs it again to fold the translations in.
Claude checks the counts and links, sends the JSON (and `threaded.txt` if asked), and sums up counts, average stars, languages, and any reply gap.
Pick **Yes, build it** on the button (or type "yes") to get the vibe dashboard from the same JSON, with no second extraction.

how_to_use_windows.step: Start the chat in the **Claude desktop app for Windows**. If it offers the built-in browser pane on your account, the steps are the same as on the Mac. This has not been tried yet, so treat the first run as a test.
If the desktop app has no browser pane, use real **Google Chrome** with the Claude in Chrome extension, or Perplexity's **Comet**. Edge and other Chromium browsers are not supported.
Paste the MakerWorld model link and say what you want: the reviews, the reviews and a dashboard, or just the text.
Approve access to makerworld.com if the browser asks. Sign in to MakerWorld yourself only if Claude reports the site refused its requests.
Claude pulls, copies out, translates, and builds the JSON exactly as on the Mac. Nothing is installed on the PC; the processing runs in Claude's workspace.
Claude sends the JSON and its summary, then the dashboard button.
Pick **Yes, build it** (or type "yes") for the vibe dashboard.

capabilities.text: Gets every rating, comment, and reply, including the ones hidden behind "View N more replies", in one run.
Reviews are public, so it normally works without a MakerWorld account.
Never posts, rates, likes, replies, boosts, downloads, or follows on Swami's behalf.
Translates Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and any other language, keeping the original text.
Every entry links straight to its thread on MakerWorld.
A dashboard can be built later from a JSON this skill made, with no new extraction.

limitations.text: Extraction needs a real browser tab: the desktop app's built-in pane, Claude in Chrome, or Comet. WebFetch and the cloud workspace can't reach makerworld.com.
Reply counts can come out a little lower than the site's, because the site still counts deleted replies.
Image-only posts come through with empty text; photos are not downloaded.
It relies on MakerWorld's own web API, which the site can change without notice.
Translations are Claude's own, with bracketed clarifications; the original text is kept beside each one.
The current version hasn't been run end to end in any browser yet; an earlier version worked in Comet.

gotchas.text: WebFetch returns an empty shell and the cloud workspace's proxy refuses makerworld.com, so don't try to fetch the page; use the browser.
Browser script calls stop after about 45 seconds. The pull runs in the background and Claude polls it; a long model just takes more polls.
Script results holding URL query strings or long encoded data come back as `[BLOCKED: …]`. The fix is built in: each chunk is written into the page as text and read back with `get_page_text`.
If the API calls fail with 401 or 403 or return nothing, sign in to MakerWorld yourself in that browser. Claude never types credentials or solves CAPTCHAs.
A fetch error is retried once after a minute. If it fails again, sign in or reload the page.
A few missing replies are normal (deleted ones still count on the site). Claude reports the gap in one line and doesn't chase it.
Use the desktop app's pane, real Chrome, or Perplexity's Comet. Edge and other Chromium browsers are not supported.
The dashboard offer comes as a button, sent last, because a file card can push a text offer out of view.

Where the file, message, or button tools aren't available (a project thread or another surface), Claude attaches the files that surface's own way and sends the summary and the dashboard offer as plain messages.
`build_reviews.py` refuses translation ids it doesn't know, so a mistyped id shows up at once instead of silently dropping a translation.
Dashboard thread tables use exactly three columns (From, Review, Link); splitting out author, stars, and date makes names break one letter per line.
Emails or phone numbers in reviews are kept as written. Claude mentions them and asks before putting them on a dashboard meant for public sharing.
The current version hasn't been run end to end yet in any browser (an earlier version worked in Comet). Treat the first run as a test and check the counts against the page.

requirements.text: A Mac, or a Windows 10 or 11 PC, with the Claude desktop app or Google Chrome with the Claude in Chrome extension.
Claude's code execution ("Create and edit files") must be on to build the JSON and the dashboard.
The browser must be allowed to open makerworld.com; Claude asks for it the first time.
Only needed if the site refuses Claude's requests; then sign in yourself in that browser.
The vibe-dashboard skill must be installed to build a reviews dashboard.

glossary.def: Bambu Lab's website for sharing 3D print models, where each model page has a Reviews & Ratings tab.
The model page's tab holding star ratings, comments, and their replies; its count includes all three.
A saved set of slicer settings attached to a MakerWorld model; each rating records which profile the reviewer printed with.
The browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, which Claude can drive; the preferred place to run the extraction.
Anthropic's extension that lets Claude act in a real Google Chrome tab; the fallback browser for this skill.
Perplexity's AI browser; supported, and the browser an earlier version of this skill ran in.
Claude's tool for reading a web page as text; it only sees an empty shell on MakerWorld, because the reviews load by script.
The browser tool that runs JavaScript in the open tab; the extraction runs through it and each call stops after about 45 seconds.
The browser tool that reads a page's text; used to copy each data chunk out of the tab.
The extraction script left running in the tab while Claude checks its progress every 35 seconds.
A piece of the extracted data, about 18,000 characters of JSON Lines, copied out of the tab one at a time.
MakerWorld's own web interface that returns reviews and replies as data; the skill calls it from inside the model page.
The Python script the skill saves and runs in Claude's workspace to thread, translate, and write the output files.
The file of English translations by entry id that the second build pass folds into the JSON.
The main output: every entry nested under its parent, with counts, notes, source details, and a flat list of the same entries.
A plain-text version of the whole thread tree in the original languages.
An entry's position in its thread: 12 is a top-level post, 12.3 a reply to it, 12.3.1 a reply to that.
A link that opens the model page at Reviews & Ratings with one thread pinned at the top, using MakerWorld's replyId and replyType.
The small shortfall between replies found and the site's reply count, caused by deleted replies the site still counts.
Swami's dark-theme single-page dashboard design; this skill can build one from the reviews JSON.
The Claude tool that shows clickable choices; used for the "Build a vibe-dashboard?" offer.
The Claude tool that delivers a file into the chat as a card.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the MakerWorld reviews skill. It pulls every rating, comment, and nested reply from a MakerWorld model page into one translated, threaded file with a working link for each entry, and it can turn that file into a vibe dashboard.
spoken.Dashboard Summary: A short intro and a table of every section
spoken.What It Is: What the skill is, and why it exists: MakerWorld loads reviews ten at a time by script, so the data has to come from the site's own interface, called from a real browser tab
spoken.What It Does: Eight things it handles: the full pull in the background, a count check, translation, the threaded file, permalinks, a plain text version, and a dashboard in the current vibe dashboard format, with search, a mind map, and a glossary
spoken.How to Use It: What to ask for, then eight steps on the Mac, from opening the desktop app and pasting the model link, to picking yes on the dashboard button. A second table gives the Windows steps, which have not been tried yet
spoken.Skills It Depends On: The built in browser skill, or the Chrome browser skill for Chrome, and the vibe dashboard skill for dashboards. The Facebook comments and YouTube comments skills are related siblings
spoken.Programs It Depends On: The Claude desktop app, Google Chrome with the Claude in Chrome extension, or Perplexity's Comet browser, plus Python in Claude's workspace. Edge and [Bambu](/bˈæmbuː/) Studio are not needed
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It gets every thread with no sign in, reads only, and translates any language. But it needs a real browser tab, does one model per run, can miss a few deleted replies, skips photos, and this version hasn't been run end to end yet
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None. The skill runs only when asked
spoken.Where It Runs: It is meant for the desktop app linked to the Mac, but this version hasn't been run end to end there yet; an earlier version worked in the Comet browser, which is supported again. Plain web and mobile sessions can only build a dashboard from an existing file, and Windows, Claude Code, and other assistants are untested
spoken.Gotchas: Thirteen traps, from the empty page that web fetch sees and the forty five second script limit, to sign in errors, unsupported browsers, and personal details in reviews
spoken.Other Requirements: A Mac or a Windows ten or eleven PC with the desktop app or Chrome, code execution, access to the site, and the vibe dashboard skill for dashboards
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint
